summary.text: A 7-year-old boy was admitted with fever and cough that persisted for 4 days. HRCT showed right middle lobe consolidation with bronchial wall thickening, tree bud signs and lobular nodules in both lungs, and the diagnosis was Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia with bronchiolitis. Past history included rhinitis.

He received intravenous methylprednisolone for 3 days and azithromycin for 7 days. At discharge he had occasional productive cough and exertional fatigue, with more prominent wet rales and a protracted expiratory phase, and HRCT showed mostly resolved consolidation but widespread bronchiolitis.

He was advised to complete azithromycin and oral prednisone for 10 days, after which he had no cough or rales but persisting exhaustion. At 28 days and again at 4 months after discharge he reported no discomfort and HRCT and pulmonary function tests had returned to normal.

summary.text: A 7-year-old boy was admitted with a 10-day history of cough, with consolidation of the right middle lobe and extensive uneven exudation on HRCT, and a diagnosis of Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia with bronchiolitis. Past history included eczema and capillary bronchitis, with prior reactions to milk, peanuts and eggs.

He received oral azithromycin for 3 days, intravenous amoxicillin-clavulanate for 6 days and budesonide atomization for 1 week. Within 2 months of discharge his cough and wheezing recurred with a few medium-fine moist rales, pulmonary function testing showed small-airway dysfunction, and HRCT showed a mosaic perfusion pattern.
He was considered to have postinfectious bronchiolitis obliterans. After retreatment for 3 months, HRCT findings did not significantly improve.

summary.text: A 7-year-old boy was admitted with a 2-week history of cough and a 3-day high fever, with a diagnosis of Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia with bronchiolitis. HRCT showed features of diffuse bronchiolitis in the anterior basal segments of the lower lobes with solid nodular shadows. Past history included atopic dermatitis.

He received azithromycin and ceftriaxone for 5 days and the cough was significantly relieved at discharge. One week later he had severe coughing after exercise, relieved by rest, with moderate moist rales; pulmonary function testing showed small-airway dysfunction that improved after bronchodilator therapy.
He was considered to have asthma and was prescribed Seretide 100 μg inhalation twice daily. HRCT after 1 month showed disappearance of the inflammation and pulmonary function returned to normal.

article_limitations: The article has no figures and no supplements.
Table 1 merges cells with row spans; the Case 2 physical-examination cell ("Any significant findings") spans two rows and its polarity is not stated.
Table 1 values carry no explicit time except the "Lung function at discharge" block; laboratory, symptom and examination rows are recorded without time.
Case 2 discharge lung-function values in Table 1 conflict with the text statement that lung function was not examined at discharge.
The statement that blood and sputum cultures were negative and biochemical parameters normal is worded for the series, so it is kept review-only per patient.
Cell values "None" in the MP PCR and MP-IgM rows do not say whether the test was not done or negative and are kept review-only.
Admission window (January 2022 to September 2022) is stated for the series, not per patient.

The discussion states that, as in "our three cases", lung function improved considerably during recovery, and that unrelated medications were given to "these three patients" because of possible mixed infections; these are not recorded as separate per-patient facts because they name no specific value, drug or time.

Table 1 has no legend or footnote; "None" is read as absent for history, allergy, symptom and examination rows and left uninterpreted (review-only) for the MP PCR and MP-IgM test rows, where it could mean not done or negative.
